# `item` commands

## `item activate`

Activate a item.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.activate` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item activate 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 2 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item activate", "input": {"item": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 2}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

## `item convert`

Convert a non-inventory part or other charge into an inventory part. One-way: it cannot be converted back. The item keeps its id, so every document still names it. Nothing posted changes: earlier purchases stay expensed and earlier sales stay without cost of goods. Stock on hand starts at 0 on the conversion date; from then on purchases put it into stock and sales relieve stock at average cost. If some is on the shelf now, count it with `inventory adjust`. Refused while an open purchase order, estimate, proposal or work order names the item. People only, with a reason; `--dry-run` previews the accounts it will carry.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.convert` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item convert "Copper Coupling" --to inventory --reason "We stock couplings now" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item convert", "input": {"item": "Copper Coupling", "to": "inventory"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | `ITEM` | string | yes | no | — | The non-inventory part or other charge to convert: ID or canonical full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `to` | `--to` | literal["inventory"] | yes | no | — | What it becomes: `inventory`, an inventory part. The only conversion there is. |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | First day the item carries stock (ISO date). Defaults to today, or to the last document using the item when that is later; it must be on or after that document, and no stock line may be dated before it afterwards. |
| `cogs_account` | `--cogs-account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Cost-of-goods-sold account its sales charge: ID or full name. Defaults to the item's expense account when that is a cost-of-goods account, else the company's only one. |
| `asset_account` | `--asset-account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Inventory asset account: ID or full name. Defaults to the company's Inventory Asset account, the only one an inventory part may use. |
| `income_account` | `--income-account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Income account its sales credit: ID or full name. Defaults to the item's own; required when the item had no sales side. |
| `description` | `--description` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Sales description. Defaults to the item's own, else its purchase description. |
| `purchase_description` | `--purchase-description` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Purchase description. Defaults to the item's own, else its sales description. |
| `price` | `--price` | any \| null | no | yes | null | Sales price. Defaults to the item's own, else 0. |
| `cost` | `--cost` | any \| null | no | yes | null | Standard purchase cost. Defaults to the item's own, else 0. Not the value of stock on hand, which starts at 0. |

| `dropped_expense_account` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The expense account its purchases posted to; an inventory part has none, so earlier documents keep it and later purchases go to stock. |
| `changed_fields` | array[string] | yes | no | — | — |
| `quantity_on_hand` | string | yes | no | — | Always 0: stock starts empty. Count what is on the shelf with `inventory adjust`. |
| `last_document_date` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | Date of the last document using the item before the conversion; null when none did. |
| `one_way` | boolean | yes | no | — | Always true: an inventory part cannot be converted back. |
| `notes` | array[string] | yes | no | — | What the conversion means, in words: one-way, history unchanged, stock starts at 0. |

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_AMOUNT_PRECISION` | The amount has more decimal places than the currency allows. |
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INACTIVE_REFERENCE` | A new or changed reference must name an active record. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_IN_USE` | The record is still used by active records. |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_TYPE_CHANGE` | That record type cannot be changed directly. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |

## `item create`

Create a item.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item create --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item create", "input": {"name": "Example subtotal", "type": "subtotal", "description": "Subtotal"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.create`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

## `item deactivate`

Deactivate a item.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.deactivate` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item deactivate 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 1 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item deactivate", "input": {"item": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 1}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `cascade` | `--cascade` | boolean | no | no | false | — |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.deactivate`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |

## `item merge`

Merge a duplicate item into another of the same type. Nothing posted changes: sales and purchases by item and every item filter show the merged item's lines under the survivor; group and assembly members, price levels and vendor profiles naming it are re-pointed to the survivor, and the merged item is made inactive and hidden. A saved document that names it saves with the survivor when next edited. People only, with a reason; `--dry-run` previews what moves, every reference re-pointed and any conflict. Undo with `item unmerge`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.merge` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item merge "Drain Clean" "Drain Cleaning" --reason "Same service entered twice" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "item merge", "input": {"merged": "Drain Clean", "into": "Drain Cleaning"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `merged` | `MERGED` | string | yes | no | — | The duplicate entry to merge away: ID or canonical full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `into` | `INTO` | string | yes | no | — | The entry it is merged into, which survives: ID or canonical full name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.merge`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `merge_id` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The merge; null only in a dry run of a new merge. |
| `changed` | boolean | yes | no | — | False when this exact merge already stands; nothing was written. |
| `merged_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `merged_name` | string | yes | no | — | — |

## `item query`

Query a bounded page of items; `query` searches by name (for example "query": "Riverside"), and `item query options` lists the filters, sorts and columns.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |

## `item unmerge`

Undo an item merge: the merged item reads as itself again, is made active again if the merge made it inactive, and every reference the merge re-pointed is put back unless it has been changed since. Nothing posted changes. People only, with a reason.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/item.unmerge` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow item unmerge "Drain Clean" --reason "Two services after all" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json

```

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_AMOUNT_PRECISION` | The amount has more decimal places than the currency allows. |
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_HIERARCHY_CYCLE` | The requested parent would create a hierarchy cycle. |
| `E_HIERARCHY_DEPTH` | The requested hierarchy would exceed the maximum depth. |
| `E_INACTIVE_REFERENCE` | A new or changed reference must name an active record. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NAME_TAKEN` | That display name is already used. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_IN_USE` | The record is still used by active records. |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_TYPE_CHANGE` | That record type cannot be changed directly. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VALUE_RANGE` | The value is outside its allowed range or storage bounds. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
